thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate detected: 5xx spike + connection resets across ingress in eu-central-1 (euc1). Potential cross-AZ routing abnormalities.

jordan: paging maya — oncall for infra. 5xx spike started ~1899997960 per alert.

maya (oncall): on it. I see surge on ALB -> envoy with a ton of `504`/`502` + `connection reset` in logs for pods in euc1b.

liam: +1. Any customer-facing routes impacted?

maya (oncall): preliminary: ~18% of traffic to /v1/generate seeing errors, affects both hosted API and some Dedicated customers in eu region. Not global yet.

sam: grabbing LB metrics now. ALB target group health trending FAIL for pod pool `inference-euc1b-1`. NLB shows SEP health ok.

ops-chris: I see BGP flaps reported to cloud provider in euc1b around the same time. Could be partial routing blackhole between AZs.

maya (oncall): checking envoy logs, lots of `recv reset` from upstream, then envoy restarts on some nodes. Suspect intermittent networking to backend pods.

eng-platform: pushing an incident tag in the console: `incident/euc1b-ingress-networking` and enabling debug logs for ingress controller.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) fail traffic away from affected AZ (euc1b) at ALB by setting target weight 0 for that AZ's targets; 2) scale up healthy pods in euc1a + euc1c; 3) if DNS split-brain suspected, force region-level route pref changes. Doing step 1 now.

jordan: keep me posted before any DNS changes. We prefer ALB weight shift first. If we can't stabilize in 10min, we'll escalate cross-region failover.

maya (oncall): executing target group weight shift.

```bash
# reduce weight for euc1b targets
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
# then set deregistration delay short, and deregister
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-abcdef
```

maya (oncall): weight shift applied. Observability: immediate drop in connections to euc1b targets. Error rate falling from 18% -> 6% within 90s.

liam: good. Are any Dedicated customers still seeing issues? Alice-cx can you confirm?

alice-cx: saw a couple of support pings but most customers report degraded latency not failures. I'll send a notice to affected customers: 'We're investigating increased errors in eu-central-1; traffic is being rerouted; we'll update.'

sam: scaling healthy pools + increasing pod anti-affinity so we don't colocate with suspect nodes. K8s rollout in progress: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/ingress-proxy -n inference --to-recreate`

ops-chris: provider says they saw an AZ control-plane glitch affecting route propagation. They've applied a repair action. They flagged possible DNS cache inconsistencies for internal load balancers.

eng-platform: adding proactive route validation and clearing internal DNS caches for envoy nodes (via sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved on bastions, and `kubectl exec` to clear cache where applicable).

maya (oncall): handing off to liam for longer-term monitoring & post-incident. I'm stepping off after 30m. Current state: error rate down to 1.2%, latency back to normal. Marking incident as Handoff.

liam: ack, taking over. I'll keep watch for 2h and coordinate with provider for RCA. Next steps: capture packet traces from affected AZ, gather kube events, and save envoy metrics.

eng-platform: exported traces and screenshots to runbook: https://redwood.internal/incident/1899998000. Added `ingress:networking` tag.

sam: saved `kubectl get events` and pod logs to s3://redwood-incidents/1899998000/logs.tar.gz

jordan: thanks team. Customer impact: partial for eu-central endpoints for ~18 minutes; no full region outage. We'll prepare a mitigation note for customers and a timeline for RCA.

liam: quick summary for paging channel: cause = cloud provider AZ route propagation flap -> intermittent upstream resets -> envoy restarts -> ALB target failures. Mitigation = ALB weight shift away from euc1b, scale healthy pools, clear internal DNS caches, provider repaired AZ routing.

alice-cx: drafting customer-facing update. Will ask PM for approvals.

eng-platform: scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Action items assigned in runbook.

maya (oncall): closing my oncall window. Leaving notes: `oncall_notes.md` in the incident runbook with exact CLI commands used.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Severity: sev2. Timeline file: https://redwood.internal/incident/1899998000/timeline.md

liam: resolved? marking as monitoring for 2h then archive.

ops-chris: provider follow-up ticket #CP-4522 created noting BGP route flap and internal LB DNS cache TTL bug.
